kept.q: In an acid-base titration, 20.0 cm3 of a sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution of unknown concentration was titrated against 0.10 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid (HCl). The reaction required 24.0 cm3 of the acid for complete neutralization. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH solution.
kept.explanation: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O, a 1:1 mole ratio. Moles of HCl = 0.024 dm3 x 0.10 mol/dm3 = 0.0024 mol, so moles of NaOH = 0.0024 mol. Concentration of NaOH = 0.0024 mol / 0.020 dm3 = 0.12 mol/dm3.
kept.pidgin: HCl and NaOH dey react 1:1. Moles of HCl = 0.024 x 0.10 = 0.0024 mol, so NaOH moles too na 0.0024 mol. Divide am by 0.020 dm3 give 0.12 mol/dm3.

kept.q: A student titrated 0.1 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid (a strong acid) against 0.1 mol/dm3 ammonia solution (a weak base). The equivalence point of this titration occurs on the acidic side of pH 7, because the salt formed (ammonium chloride) hydrolyses to give an acidic solution. Which indicator is most suitable for detecting the end point of this titration?
kept.explanation: Methyl orange changes colour within the acidic pH range (about 3.1 to 4.4), which matches where the equivalence point of a strong acid-weak base titration occurs. Phenolphthalein changes colour in the alkaline range, so it is not suitable here.
kept.pidgin: Methyl orange dey change colour for acidic pH range (3.1 to 4.4), and dat na where strong acid-weak base titration equivalence point dey. Phenolphthalein dey change for alkaline side, so e no fit work well here.

kept.q: 25 cm3 of a solution containing 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide per dm3 was titrated against 0.2 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid. Calculate the volume of the acid required for complete neutralization. (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
kept.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol, so concentration of NaOH = 4.0/40 = 0.1 mol/dm3. Moles of NaOH in 25 cm3 = 0.1 x 0.025 = 0.0025 mol, equal to moles of HCl needed (1:1 ratio). Volume of HCl = 0.0025 mol / 0.2 mol/dm3 = 0.0125 dm3 = 12.5 cm3.
kept.pidgin: NaOH molar mass na 40, so concentration = 4.0/40 = 0.1 mol/dm3. Moles for 25cm3 = 0.1 x 0.025 = 0.0025 mol, na im HCl moles too (1:1). Volume = 0.0025/0.2 = 0.0125 dm3 wey be 12.5 cm3.

kept.q: 20 cm3 of 0.05 mol/dm3 sulphuric acid (H2SO4) was used to completely neutralize 25 cm3 of a sodium hydroxide solution. Given the equation H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O, calculate the concentration of the NaOH solution.
kept.explanation: Moles of H2SO4 = 0.020 dm3 x 0.05 mol/dm3 = 0.0010 mol. Since the ratio of NaOH to H2SO4 is 2:1, moles of NaOH = 2 x 0.0010 = 0.0020 mol. Concentration of NaOH = 0.0020 mol / 0.025 dm3 = 0.08 mol/dm3.
kept.pidgin: H2SO4 moles = 0.020 x 0.05 = 0.0010 mol. Since NaOH to H2SO4 ratio na 2:1, NaOH moles = 2 x 0.0010 = 0.0020 mol. Concentration = 0.0020/0.025 = 0.08 mol/dm3.

kept.q: 25 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), Na2CO3, solution was titrated with 0.2 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid, according to the equation Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Calculate the volume of HCl required for complete reaction.
kept.explanation: Moles of Na2CO3 = 0.025 dm3 x 0.1 mol/dm3 = 0.0025 mol. From the equation, moles of HCl needed = 2 x 0.0025 = 0.0050 mol. Volume of HCl = 0.0050 mol / 0.2 mol/dm3 = 0.025 dm3 = 25.0 cm3.
kept.pidgin: Na2CO3 moles = 0.025 x 0.1 = 0.0025 mol. From the equation, HCl wey dem need = 2 x 0.0025 = 0.0050 mol. Volume = 0.0050/0.2 = 0.025 dm3 wey be 25.0 cm3.

kept.q: A student dissolved 2.0 g of an impure sample of sodium hydroxide in distilled water and made the solution up to 250 cm3 in a volumetric flask. 25 cm3 of this solution required 20 cm3 of 0.15 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid for complete neutralization. Calculate the percentage purity of the NaOH sample. (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
kept.explanation: Moles of HCl used = 0.020 x 0.15 = 0.0030 mol, which equals moles of NaOH in the 25 cm3 sample (1:1 ratio). Scaling up to 250 cm3 (x10), total moles of pure NaOH = 0.030 mol, giving a mass of 0.030 x 40 = 1.2 g. Percentage purity = (1.2/2.0) x 100 = 60%.
